sources.title: Deterministic Batch 0059 RPC candidate source/shape validation

claims.text: The two frozen source variants ask for an RPC framework at a stated 100k target but use different units, 100k OPS and 100k QPS, and preserve Netty, serialization, service-governance/load-balancing and high-performance-call concerns; they do not provide a production payload mix, node count, hardware profile, percentile SLO or measured per-instance throughput.

The candidate keeps QPS and OPS distinct, decomposes the end-to-end latency budget instead of using an average-only claim, and computes instance requirements from measured safe per-instance throughput plus failure-domain survival and headroom rather than inventing universal Netty or hardware capacity.

The candidate uses Netty-style event loops for connection/IO state progression while keeping uncontrollable blocking business, storage and downstream work behind a bounded worker or asynchronous boundary, and makes event-loop utilization/lag and worker saturation separate observability/capacity dimensions.

The candidate reuses persistent connection/channel state, models request correlation and bounded in-flight state explicitly, versions the RPC protocol/codec, and treats serialization/native transport as workload-measured optimizations rather than unconditional performance winners.

The candidate separates name resolution/discovery, endpoint health/readiness and load-balancing selection, and puts per-method deadline/retry policy in the framework/control-plane contract instead of scattering it through business call sites.

The candidate propagates a bounded end-to-end time budget, allows retries only for classified failures with remaining deadline/attempt budget and a safe idempotency boundary, and uses bounded in-flight/worker queues plus flow control or fast rejection to prevent retry/queue amplification during overload.

The candidate treats endpoint draining, reconnect jitter, protocol/codec compatibility, steady-state plus overload/failover testing and per-method tail-latency/resource observability as part of the proof for the 100k/millisecond target, and explicitly refuses to fabricate company-specific topology, node counts or production latency numbers.
